steps.label: mc.global census: dprc.0 holds only dprc.1
steps.expect: zero exit; expect exactly one row — dprc.1, listed unplugged. Confirms the answered half of dprc.md unknown 5: the MC's own container (dprc.0, aliased mc.global) holds only the root container

steps.label: read the MC's own container attributes
steps.expect: exit any; the open half of dprc.md unknown 5 — is an attribute read against the MC's own container (dprc.0) accepted at all? Capture the id/icid/portal/options surface if it succeeds, or the MC status text verbatim if it is refused

steps.label: resource walk on dprc.0
steps.expect: exit any; record whether the pooled-resource walk is accepted on dprc.0. --resources is absent from restool's help text but exists in v2.4 (dprc_commands.c); when accepted it lists the container's resources by type

steps.label: PEB free-block dump on the root container
steps.expect: exit any; dprc.md unknown 10 — the Packet-Express-Buffer partition's free-block output semantics on this firmware. Capture the block listing

steps.label: PEB free-block dump on the MC's own container
steps.expect: exit any; the same PEB dump against dprc.0 — whether the partition query is answered there too, and how its output differs from the root's

steps.label: dpmcp.14 is a plugged root resident, not an id hole
steps.expect: zero exit; dpmcp.14 reads back present in the root container — a consumed dpmcp companion, not a gap. Corrects the 'id hole at 14' premise from 5.5 (dprc.md unknown 7): the id is occupied, so the hole is a wrong reading of the pool, folded here rather than left open

steps.label: /dev/dprc.N node mode and owner
steps.expect: exit any; dprc.md unknown 11 (mode/owner) — capture the /dev/dprc.N node's permission bits and owner:group. The kernel sets no mode on the misc device by default, so anything relaxed here is this BSP's udev, which decides whether the Rust portal needs root or CAP_NET_ADMIN only

steps.label: udev rules mentioning dprc
steps.expect: zero exit (guarded by '; true'); unknown 11's udev half — whether any udev rule mentions dprc. Empty output (no match) is the expected answer on a stock BSP and means the kernel default mode stands

steps.label: child-DPRC autorescan state
steps.expect: zero exit; dprc.md unknown 12 — whether child-DPRC IRQ autorescan is enabled in this BSP. 1 means child-container mutations become visible without an explicit rescan by the mutator; 0 means they do not
